title: Cold War Crises Adventure
welcome_lead: Today you'll feel the heat of Hungary 1956, Berlin 1961 and Cuba 1962.
meta_desc: GCSE History — Warsaw Pact, Hungary, Berlin Wall and Cuban Missile Crisis.
final_note: You learned how the world came within hours of nuclear war in October 1962.

concepts.def: Built overnight 13 August 1961 to stop defections
April 1961 failed US-backed invasion of Cuba
13-day standoff in October 1962 over Soviet missiles

walkthroughs.body_html:
In 1955 the USSR formed the Warsaw Pact after West Germany joined NATO.

In October 1956 Hungarians overthrew their Stalinist regime. PM Imre Nagy announced free elections and withdrawal from the Pact. Khrushchev sent 200,000 troops and 1,000 tanks. Nagy was hanged in 1958.

Between 1949 and 1961, 2.7 million East Germans fled through West Berlin.

Overnight on 13 August 1961 the GDR built the Berlin Wall. Kennedy gave his 'Ich bin ein Berliner' speech in 1963. The Wall became the symbol of a divided world.

After Castro's revolution and the failed Bay of Pigs (April 1961), Khrushchev placed nuclear missiles in Cuba.

U-2 photos exposed them on 14 October 1962. Kennedy blockaded the island. After 13 days, Khrushchev removed the missiles in return for a secret US pledge to remove missiles from Turkey.
